nodes.name: Hydrothermal, Annealing and Acid Wash for Sample C
nodes.procedure: Mixing of Ru, Mn, Ca, and Pr precursors followed by hydrothermal treatment at 25-60 C for 6-24 hours. The resulting material was then annealed at 400-500 C for 6 hours. Finally, the product underwent an acid wash process to obtain the final catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM shows sample C consists of single-crystalline RuO2 particles (~5-10 nm) forming a polycrystalline structure. The (110) lattice spacing expanded to 3.25 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) results ... sample C's lattice spacing of the (110) lattice plane expanded to 3.25Å when compared to the standard lattice spacing of the pure Ru samples

properties.description: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image showing morphology of the sample.

properties.observation: Lattice expansion observed upon Mn doping

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of dopants (Mn, Ca, Pr) in the major RuO2 lattice of sample C without aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequent energy-dispersive x-ray analysis via TEM in Fig. 5D further strengthened our belief that the second to fourth metal elements are uniformly distributed ... suggesting their existence as dopants in the major RuO2 lattice.

properties.spatial_distribution: Homogeneous distribution of elements across the nanostructure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms RuO2 as the main phase for sample C with peak shifts indicating lattice expansion. Absence of perovskite impurities like SrRuO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Having been acid washed, sample C seemed to be dominated by the RuO2 phase (Fig. 5E) ... no traces of CaRuO3 and SrRuO3 could be found like that in A/B/D.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Mn as a dopant and shows that sample C has the highest Ru>4+ species ratio (35.24%), enhancing charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS Mn-2p spectra ... indicates Mn cation's difference with that in Mn oxides and as a dopant ... sample C has the highest ratio (35.24%) among A to D.

visual_evidence.name: XPS Analysis of Ru oxidation states

nodes.characterization_summary: Sample B exhibits the highest BET surface area of 94.35 m2/g, followed by A (88.88), D (74.47), and C (39.92). RuO2-500 baseline was 45.58 m2/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: sample B exhibits the highest Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 94.35 m2 g−1, greater than that of A at 88.88 ... D at 74.47 ... and C at 39.92 ... RuO2-500 ... has a notably low BET surface area of 45.58 m2 g−1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) was used to compare magnetic properties and support the doping of Mn into the Ru oxide lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This was further supported by electron paramagnetic resonance comparisons of magnetic properties (fig. S31).

nodes.characterization_summary: Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) quantitative analysis, combined with XPS, confirmed Mn as the major dopant in Sample C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Combining the XPS semi- and inductively coupled plasma quantitative analysis summarized in fig. S30, we confirmed that Mn was the major dopant.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) on MEAs showed Sample C had lower contact, charge transfer, and mass transfer resistances than A/B/D.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy conducted on the corresponding MEA samples (fig. S23), verified that sample C ... exhibited comparatively lower contact, charge transfer, and mass transfer resistances
